questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How individuals can recycle more at home
The idea of shrinking parts of the economy to fight climate change
Why economies grow faster in some countries
How new technology is creating more jobs
questions.why: Phil and Hannah discuss degrowth – the idea that we should stop economies growing to tackle the climate crisis.

questions.q: What does Phil say about his own habits?
options: He never drives and always recycles
He thinks individuals can't do anything useful, so he doesn't try
He has stopped buying new clothes
He cycles and recycles, but feels he should do more
questions.why: Phil says he cycles more than he drives and recycles, but 'should be doing a lot more'.

questions.q: According to Hannah, what do some people think about dealing with climate change?
options: We must change how the economy works, not just rely on individuals
Individuals should do everything themselves
Governments should leave it to scientists
It will be solved naturally by economic growth and by new technology
questions.why: She says we can't just rely on individuals and need to change the way our economy works.

options: To reduce the number of jobs
To use fewer of the Earth's natural resources and make less stuff
To grow the economy with more money, jobs and goods
To stop people buying cheap clothes
questions.why: Hannah says governments have always wanted to grow the economy: 'more money, more jobs and more stuff'.

questions.q: According to journalist Alvaro Alvarez, what does degrowth really mean?
options: Reducing everything we make and buy by about half over ten years
Stopping all production of food
Closing all factories in rich countries
Cutting only the kinds of production that aren't useful
questions.why: He says it's not about reducing everything, but decreasing elements of production that are not beneficial.

questions.q: Which example does Alvaro NOT give of something degrowth would reduce?
options: Public transport
Fast fashion
Private jets
The beef and meat industry
questions.why: His examples are fast fashion, private jets and the beef and meat industry.

questions.q: Why does Hannah say 'before we go any further' and mention economists?
options: To show that most economists now strongly support the idea of degrowth
To explain how degrowth started
To make it clear that many experts disagree with the idea
To introduce a new solution to poverty
questions.why: She points out that many economists don't think degrowth is a good idea and say it could create more poverty.

questions.q: What is Professor Sam Fankhauser's main criticism of degrowth?
options: It would make fashion too expensive
It doesn't value new technology and investment enough
It is far too similar to what governments are already doing today
It focuses too much on individuals
questions.why: He says degrowth underestimates the power of innovation and the need for investment in new technology.
